summary: Curry County lookout house on the summit by 1934, with no tower; activated 1942, and the site page later lists it as removed, with no date.

facts.design: House on the summit, no tower (as described in 1934)
facts.status_note: The site page's last entry is 'Removed', with no date given.

events.note: First documented in late April 1934 (visit of April 26, 1934) as a house on the summit. The April 1933 report discusses only a plan. Exact build date unknown.
Activated August 30, 1942, naming the Roseburg Filter Center. On September 11, 1942, an AWS inspector reported a 20x22 portable building completed.

evidence.supports: April 7, 1933 field report (P.S. King): writer wished to talk with Demar Colegrove about a lookout on the high point
evidence.quote: We stopped to see Demar Colegrove as I wished to talk to him about putting a lookout on that high point

evidence.supports: April 26, 1934 visit: lookout on Mr. Colegrove's land
evidence.quote: looked at the lookout on Mr. Colegrove's land

evidence.supports: April 26, 1934: no tower; house set tight on top of the mountain
evidence.quote: they made no tower but set the house tight on top of the mountain

evidence.supports: April 26, 1934: view to the north obstructed about fifty per cent
evidence.quote: the vision to the north is obstructed about fifty per cent

evidence.supports: June 12, 1934 entry (P.S. King): good standard lookout house; felling the north-side timber gives good visibility for the entire country
evidence.quote: They have built a good standard lookout house and have felled the timber on the north side which gives it good visibility for the entire country

evidence.supports: June 14, 1934 Curry County Reporter: lookout cabins erected in the county (page lists Colegrove Butte under a CURRY COUNTY heading)
evidence.quote: Several new lookout cabins have been erected in the county during the past year

evidence.supports: June 14, 1934 Curry County Reporter: one lookout built on Colegrove Butte near the Oregon Coast Highway
evidence.quote: One has been built on Colegrove Butte, near the Oregon Coast Highway

evidence.supports: June 14, 1934 Reporter: site a quarter mile back from the road to Brookings
evidence.quote: being only a quarter of a mile back from the road between here and Brookings

evidence.supports: June 14, 1934 Reporter: Stanley Colegrove expected to be the first observer
evidence.quote: It is reported that Stanley Colegrove will be the first observer to occupy this post.

evidence.supports: September 11, 1942: AWS inspector W.N. Parke reports a 20x22 portable building completed
evidence.quote: September 11, 1942: A report by W.N. Parke, AWS Inspector, stated that a 20x22 portable building, sealed and double walled, had been completed.

notes_for_editor: Single source: a hobbyist site that quotes 1933-1942 field reports and a 1934 Curry County Reporter item. No agency, register or current-condition source found; two web searches returned nothing on the site today. The 'Removed' entry has no date, so no removal event is written. The build year 1934 is the first documented year, not a confirmed build date. Record status and kind stay unknown in the record; not corrected here because the source only supports removed status and a house with no tower in 1934. The Coos FPA label on the page is not explained and is not used.
